definition: An alignment algorithm that optimizes an implicit reward function directly via cross-entropy loss without training a separate reward model or using reinforcement learning.
details: DPO parameterizes the reward model directly through the policy model itself, avoiding the instability, hyperparameter tuning overhead, and high computational cost associated with standard PPO pipelines.
story: Picture guardrails on a mountain road — not there to slow you down on the straightaways, but to keep you from flying off the cliff. It is the habit of asking, before every launch, what could go wrong — and then doing something about it. Think of it as the quiet rule that a tool should be useful without being dangerous. It is the difference between “it works” and “it is safe to put in front of people.” That deliberate caution is Direct Preference Optimization.

citation.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model Is Secretly a Reward Model
citation.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
